citation: [Pomeroy house, 1824 S. Prairie Avenue, in its original Italianate form.] Unknown photographer, undated (before the stone front of about 1880). Reproduced on the Glessner House Museum's blog 'The Story of a House' ('The early history of Prairie Avenue', June 2020); chicagology.com's 1824 Prairie page reproduces the same photograph, slightly wider.
author: unknown photographer
describes_date: between 1857, when the house was built, and the stone front George B. Marsh gave it soon after buying it in 1880
repository: Glessner House Museum (reproduced on its blog without a rights statement; the original holder is not named). Prairie library images a18-gh-pomeroy-house-italianate (the blog's copy) and cgn-1824-pomeroy-italianate-copy (Chicagology's, the same photograph), both 'link only'; the project reads the image store's copies (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/<id>.jpg). No copy is committed here: no camera is solved from it yet.
locator: The house from the east side of Prairie Avenue, obliquely: the main block's two tall storeys over a raised basement under a bracketed cornice and a low hip with a square cupola; an arcaded porch with a balustraded deck; the entrance up a curved stoop at the right; a lower two-storey block with its own bracketed hip and two stacks at the left; an ornamental iron fence along the walk. The blog's text beside it: 'featuring an elaborate bracketed cornice, front and side porches, and a large cupola ... In 1880, it was purchased by George B. Marsh and soon after received an entirely new stone façade.'
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms, counts and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset, and no copy is committed.

note: The one picture of the 1857 villa. It is a picture of the house BEFORE its 1880s stone front, so it is read only for what that front did not change: the storeys and the raised basement, the bracketed cornice and its deep eave, the low hip, the lower block beside the main one, the stacks and the flanks' round-headed windows under hoods. Its front, its arcaded porch and its cupola are evidence of the 1860s and 1870s, not of 1904 (the register's phase guard).
what_it_supplies: the villa's storeys over a raised basement, its bracketed cornice and deep eave, its low hip roof
the lower two-storey block beside the main one, under its own bracketed hip
